Subject: Access controls follow-up 1 RBAC, support access, break-glass

Hi Alex 1 thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps on the access controls items we discussed:

1) RBAC & least-privilege model
- Redwood supports role-based access controls at the org, project, and environment level.
- Built-in roles: Admin, Billing, Developer, ReadOnly, Support (scoped). Custom roles via policy API are possible.

2) Support access & break-glass
- Support access is restricted by default; we only grant short-lived support sessions (timeboxed) and require customer approval for break-glass events.
- All sessions are logged, recorded in audit trails, and tied to an incident ticket.

3) Logging & retention
- Audit logs capture user, action, resource, timestamp, and originating IP. Logs can be exported to your SIEM.
- Default retention is 90 days for audit logs on hosted accounts; we support extended retention packages and on-prem options for Private deployments.

4) Data residency & PII handling
- We can pin data to specific regions; we also offer a Private deployment option if you need an air-gapped environment.
- For PII: Redwood supports field-level redaction, query-time masking, and configurable retention policies 1 we need your PII classification and retention windows to provide concrete recommendations.

Next steps:
- Could you confirm which data classes you consider PII and required retention windows? (e.g., 30/90/365 days or custom)
- Would you like a short technical deep-dive with our infra lead (Dev) next week to go over RBAC policies, break-glass workflows, and log export?

I attached a one-pager that summarizes our RBAC model. Happy to add more detail in the next call.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192

Thanks Marissa 1 helpful summary. A few clarifying questions from our security team (see attached questionnaire):

- For support break-glass, what is the escalation path and who needs to approve? Is approval single-person or multi-person (we prefer two-person approval for elevated access).
- Can we require MFA for all support sessions and tie session approvals to specific groups in our IdP (Okta)?
- For audit logs: can you guarantee immutability or ship to our S3 bucket/CloudWatch for retention and legal hold?
- PII classification: our initial list is attached (PII_Classes tab). Most of our models will process account numbers and partial SSNs; retention for those should be 180 days unless under legal hold.

Attached: FinTrust_SecQuestionnaire.xlsx

Alex

Hi Alex and team 1 thanks for the clear asks, I've reviewed the questionnaire and outlined answers below (high level):

- Break-glass multi-approver: Our platform supports policy-driven break-glass flows. By default, support requests require a single approver, but for enterprise Dedicated/Private customers we can configure a two-person approval flow via our policy engine and integrate with your IdP for approver arbitration. We'll demo the configuration in the deep-dive.

- MFA & IdP gating: We support enforcing MFA for all support sessions. We can map approver roles to Okta groups and require group membership + MFA for approval.

- Audit logs & immutability: For Hosted accounts we can stream audit logs to customer-owned S3 buckets or to CloudWatch. For stronger immutability guarantees (object-lock/WORM), Dedicated/Private deployments are the recommended path; we can discuss a retention + legal-hold playbook in the call.

- PII retention: 180 days for account numbers/partial SSNs is feasible. We recommend applying field-level masking plus a retention policy that automatically purges sensitive artifacts. For legal hold, we can mark records and override purge on a per-case basis.

I'll schedule the deep-dive for Tue 2026-11-09 10:00 AM ET / 7:00 AM PT and send an invite. Please confirm if that works for you and whether you'd like pre-read docs 1 I can attach our RBAC summary and the break-glass playbook.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Infra Lead, Platform Security | Redwood Inference
